nodes.summary: For an odd number $d$ and a nonempty set $B$ of its primes, the Rédei matrix of $d_B$ is the Laplacian $L_B$ of the bits $a_{qp}=[p/q]$ of $d$, bordered by the column $z_B$ exactly when $y(B)=0$. Its kernel is $\{0,e_{d_B}\}$ exactly when $g_d(B)=1$. The first two articles prove the last statement for arbitrary bits satisfying reciprocity; the others identify the Rédei matrix of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d_B})$ with the…
nodes.title: From the Rédei matrix to Rédei's bits

nodes.summary: The hypothesis CR₃^TYZ_Cl is the following assertion. Let $d$ be squarefree with $d\equiv5\pmod8$. If $|\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)|=8$ and the genus sum of class numbers $T^{\rm Cl}_{5b}(d)$ is $1$, then for every $(a,b)\in\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)$ the 2-covering $D_{a,b}$ of $C_d$ has a rational point; that is, every 2-Selmer class of $C_d$ comes from a rational point.
nodes.title: The certified rank hypothesis with class numbers

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$ and a set $B$ of primes of $d$, the product $d_B=\prod_{p\in B}p$ is a positive integer, so its genus class number $g(d_B)$ is defined. The *genus sum of class numbers* of row 5b is the sum over the set partitions $\pi$ of the primes of $d$ with exactly one block $B$ having $d_B\equiv7\pmod8$, exactly one having $d_B\equiv3\pmod8$, and every block having $d_B\equiv7$, $3$ or $1\pmod8$.…
nodes.title: The genus sum of class numbers

nodes.summary: The hypothesis CR₃^TYZ_Cl, stated with Tian, Yuan and Zhang's genus class numbers $g(d_B)$, holds if and only if the hypothesis CR₃^TYZ, stated with Rédei's $g_d(B)$, holds. Along the way, the same equivalence is proved from Rédei's formula taken as an assumption, and from the 4-rank statement taken as an assumption.
nodes.title: CR₃ with class numbers is CR₃^TYZ

nodes.summary: As in the rest of the chapter, $n\ge1$ is an integer and $K=\mathbb Q(\omega)$ with $\omega^2=-n$; $\mathcal O$ is its ring of integers, $\sigma$ its nontrivial automorphism and $N$ the norm of elements and of ideals. This section collects what the genus theory of the next section needs about $K$:
nodes.title: The field $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ and its primes

nodes.summary: Let $n>1$ be odd and squarefree, $t=|T_n|$, and let $\chi:\mathrm{Cl}\to\mathbb F_2^{\{q\mid n\}}$ be the genus map, $c\mapsto(\chi_q(c))_q$. Counting gives so the principal genus theorem $\mathrm{Cl}^2=\bigcap_q\ker\chi_q$ holds and $|\mathrm{Cl}[2]|=2^{t-1}$. nodes.title: The 4-rank

nodes.summary: This section is the genus theory of $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$, in the notation of the chapter: $\mathcal O$, $\sigma$, $N$, $\mathrm{Cl}$, the set $T_n$ with $t=|T_n|$, the prime ideals $\mathfrak p_p$ and the residue bits $[a/q]$. The main results assume $n$ odd and squarefree; each article states its own hypotheses, and some auxiliary facts hold for every $n\ge1$.
nodes.title: Ambiguous classes and genus characters

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ let $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ be the quadratic algebra $\mathbb Q[\omega]/(\omega^2+n)$. For $n\ge1$ the number $-n$ is not a square in $\mathbb Q$, so $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ is a field, and a number field. For $n\ge1$ let $\mathrm{Cl}$ be the class group of the ring of integers of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$. The *genus class number* of $n$ is the order of the subgroup of squares…
nodes.title: The genus class number

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be odd and squarefree. Then the genus sum of row 5b with the genus class numbers $g(d_B)$ equals the genus sum with Rédei's $g_d(B)$. Along the way, the same identity is proved for every odd squarefree $d$ from Rédei's formula taken as an assumption.
nodes.title: The genus sum of class numbers is the genus sum of Rédei bits

nodes.summary: *Rédei's formula* is the following assertion. Let $d$ be odd and squarefree, and let $B$ be a nonempty set of primes of $d$ whose product $d_B=\prod_{p\in B}p$ satisfies $d_B\equiv7$, $3$ or $1\pmod8$. Then where $g(d_B)$ is the genus class number of $d_B$, the order of the subgroup of squares of the class group of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d_B})$, and $g_d(B)\in\mathbb F_2$ is Rédei's $g$ of $B$ for the bits $a_{pq}$,…
nodes.title: The statement of Rédei's formula

nodes.summary: Rédei's formula holds. Let $d$ be odd and squarefree, and let $B$ be a nonempty set of primes of $d$ with $d_B=\prod_{p\in B}p\equiv7$, $3$ or $1\pmod8$. Then the parity of the order of the subgroup of squares of the class group of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d_B})$ is Rédei's $g$ of $B$, computed from the residue bits of the primes of $d$.
nodes.title: Rédei's formula

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $T_n$ its set of ramified primes: the primes of $n$, together with $2$ unless $n\equiv3\pmod4$. The *Rédei matrix* $R$ of $n$ is the matrix over $\mathbb F_2$ with rows indexed by the primes $q\mid n$ and columns by $T_n$, with entries where $[a/q]\in\mathbb F_2$ is the residue bit.
